description: Fresh fixed Node check for pending configuration proposal admission. Three independent single-voter producer histories compare no Advance, early Advance with deferred activation, and activation before Advance. The same one-way oracle observes each second proposal entry and only requires rejection when first activation is pending. Final cleanup preserves activation order and records controlled endpoints.

harness.description: Public Node API, actual elections/proposals, MemoryStorage Ready persistence and explicit finite configuration application policies.
semantic_changes: MemoryStorage substitutes for device persistence under a no-crash model.
New peers are absent and outbound network messages are dropped.
Caller booleans record returned configuration activation calls; public Status is an event-loop processing barrier. No target code or dependency substitutions.

legality.derivation: Use public RestartNode, Campaign, ProposeConfChange, Ready, Advance, ApplyConfChange and Status. Initialize a common valid committed snapshot prefix in MemoryStorage at index/term 1 with sole voter 1 and Applied 1; a real election appends and applies its noop before actual add-voter proposals. Complete every Ready persistence before Advance, drop outbound traffic to absent new peers, and use Status as a serialized event-loop barrier. The explicit Node usage step 4 permits Advance any time after persistence step 1; configuration activation is step 3. Deferred activation is finite: after observing the second result the early policy activates first then second in committed Ready order. The no-Advance policy activates first only after the second proposal processing barrier, and then drains the resulting entry. The activated control applies first before proposing second. No private raft state is assigned or read.
legality.applicability: Synchronous public Node with default configuration validation enabled, no joint state, no crashes or role changes in the observed interval. MemoryStorage substitutes for disk with no crash; unavailable new peers are an explicit network policy. Application order is preserved across Ready batches. Five-second context bounds technical waiting, not liveness. Each subtest is an independent history.
unresolved: Node.ApplyConfChange whenever observed might be read as requiring immediate activation before Advance. The check selects the explicit numbered Node step-order permission; this interpretation must be assessed during correspondence.
alternatives: RawNode and asynchronous storage workers have distinct completion duties; their stricter wording is not used to define this Node schedule.
Tests applying configurations before Advance illustrate a safe caller policy without testing the broader documented permission.

grounding.derivation: The accepted claim requires dropping a subsequent configuration proposal while a prior committed change is neither activated nor rejected. The driver independently records activation only after an actual ApplyConfChange returns, and never rejects the first change. A Status call following ProposeConfChange completes after processing in the same serialized Node loop; no application call occurs between admission and that barrier. The result inspects the actual next emitted log entry Type, not proposal return success or internal applied. There is exactly one second proposal, with no concurrent proposal, tick, role change or inbound network message; its next emitted entry is uniquely associated with that request. Both configuration entry types count as acceptance. Empty normal substitution satisfies the required rejection.
grounding.applicability: Stable operation identity op/node/proposal_seq is on each prerequisite and result, independent of activation and compared entry type. The first committed prerequisite and proposal admission are correlated by first_index. The implication antecedent is first_pending_at_processing, independently captured from the caller activation ledger after the processing barrier; it is not inferred from the result. Activation-first control makes the implication vacuous and does not assert successful acceptance.
unresolved: Same selected Node early-Advance interpretation as Harness legality; a contrary applicability ruling would limit attribution, not change the measured entry type.
alternatives: A direct error/drop is another conforming outcome; this bounded driver reports any proposal error as technical incompletion, not as a violation. The captured implementation substitutes an empty normal entry in the pending guard path.
Commitment and final voter sets are diagnostics only, not proof of a consensus failure or eventual progress.

observable_properties.description: If the prior committed configuration has not been activated or rejected when the second proposal is processed, that second proposal must not be admitted as a configuration log entry.

uncertainties: The Node early-Advance permission and mandatory ApplyConfChange wording require correspondence review; observations alone do not settle normative precedence.
Only the selected no-crash simple-configuration admission interval is checked. No divergent decisions, crash durability or general liveness property is tested.
A direct proposal error produces driver incompletion, not a false violation; no timeout means rejection oracle is used.
